title: Implement cost-aware hybrid prefilter sampler to cut tracing hotpath overhead
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: Tracing hotpath allocations and span churn from high-QPS inference routes are increasing tail latency and CPU usage on the runtime path. Prior sampling approaches either add too much CPU (heavy tail-analysis) or lose fidelity for model/route-specific regressions.

Proposal: Introduce a cost-aware hybrid prefilter sampler that combines a super-cheap, deterministic prefilter on the request hotpath with a lightweight reservoir/tiered tail sampler in the background worker. Key pieces: 
1) Hotpath prefilter: compute a single 8-bit hash + two cheap heuristics (model_variant, token_estimate bucket) to decide quick-allow / quick-drop / candidate-for-reservoir. This prefilter must execute with zero allocations and O(1) CPU.
2) Cost weight: annotate ingress request with a small integer "cost_score" (derived from model variant, prompt length, and requested max tokens). Routes with higher cost_score increase reservoir priority so we keep proportional representation.
3) Background reservoir & tail sampler: candidate traces are committed to an async reservoir which runs tail detection and retains heavy tails and error traces for full capture. Background worker performs span encoding and enrichment off the hotpath.
4) Always-sample rules: errors (status >= 500), explicit user debug flags, and governance events (rollout signals) are always sampled.
5) Observability: add metrics for prefilter drop rate, reservoir admit rate, average per-request sampling decision latency, span allocation rate, and sampled-trace-per-route. Dashboards will show sampling coverage vs error rate and route-level CPU savings.

Trade-offs & rationale: The hybrid design minimizes hotpath overhead while preserving the ability to detect tail latency regressions across model variants and routes. Prefilter heuristics risk bias; using cost-weight normalization ensures heavy requests are proportionally represented. Offloading encoding to background workers increases complexity and requires reliable backpressure but keeps runtime latency tight.

Rollout plan: staged canary on 10% of traffic for 48h -> 50% 72h -> 100% if metrics stable. Canary will include traffic split by region and by model family to validate fairness.

Links: Design doc (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/design/cost-aware-hybrid-sampler, Spike PR (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1246
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath sampling decision added to ingress with zero heap allocations (verified via flame graphs and allocator traces)
End-to-end reduction in runtime CPU from tracing by >= 30% on high-QPS routes in staging
Error traces and p99+ latency traces retained at >= 95% fidelity compared to baseline sampling for the same window
Observability metrics and dashboards for sampling rates, admit/drop by route, and span allocations deployed in Console
Canary rollout plan executed and documented with rollback triggers defined (error rate delta > 0.5% or CPU improvement < 10%)
